classification.difficultyReason: Coordinate feature analysis with exact surd intercepts and reflected completed-square forms.

content.prompt: Follow the steps in Question 1 to sketch these quadratics: identify the concavity, $y$-intercept, axis and vertex; explain why there are $x$-intercepts and calculate them by putting $y=0$; then sketch each graph showing all key features. The $x$-intercepts involve surds.

answer.worked:
The parabola is concave up, with axis $x=-1$ and vertex $(-1,-3)$.
$$\begin{align*}y(0)&=(0+1)^2-3\\y(0)&=-2\end{align*}$$
Its vertex is below the $x$-axis and it opens upwards, so there are two intercepts.
$$\begin{align*}0&=(x+1)^2-3\\(x+1)^2&=3\\x+1&=\pm\sqrt3\\x&=-1\pm\sqrt3\end{align*}$$
Plot the vertex and intercepts and draw a smooth curve symmetric about $x=-1$.

spec.description: Equation-driven answer graph with exact surd intercept labels.
